question: Should OpenClaw adopt RFC 0018’s opt-in readiness contract, including its activation boundary, required/advisory aggregation, subject identity package, and activation-scoped plugin-provider model?
rationale: These choices define a new public configuration and plugin contract; source review can assess clarity and compatibility constraints but cannot select the long-term product boundary without maintainer intent.

options.title: Discuss and narrow before acceptance
options.body: Create the required maintainer-discussion thread, explicitly resolve the four contract choices, and amend the RFC with the accepted boundary before merge.

options.title: Defer the readiness contract
options.body: Leave the RFC draft and do not merge it until a maintainer sponsors a smaller or different readiness direction.

recommendation.title: Discuss and narrow before acceptance
recommendation.body: Create the required maintainer-discussion thread, explicitly resolve the four contract choices, and amend the RFC with the accepted boundary before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the only evidence-backed contact connecting the RFC and the linked readiness implementation stack, so they can consolidate questions for the maintainer discussion.
